statement: The supplied sources contain no derivation; they define a whitening transformation as a linear transformation $Y = W X$ (or $Y = W(X - \mu)$ if $X$ has non-zero mean $\mu$) of a random vector $X$ with non-singular covariance matrix $\Sigma$ into a whitened random vector $Y$ with identity covariance matrix (unit diagonal covariance), where the whitening matrix $W$ satisfies the condition $W^{\mathrm{T}} W = \Sigma^{-1}$.

symbols.meaning: whitened random vector with unit diagonal covariance

properties.property: The covariance of the transformed vector Y is the identity matrix, meaning its components are uncorrelated and each has variance 1.
properties.why: Follows directly from the definition of whitening transformation satisfying W^T W = \Sigma^{-1}.

properties.property: There exist infinitely many possible whitening matrices W satisfying W^T W = \Sigma^{-1}.
properties.why: Any matrix W satisfying the quadratic condition yields a valid whitening transform.

properties.property: ZCA (Mahalanobis) whitening uses the symmetric choice W = \Sigma^{-1/2}.
properties.why: Commonly used matrix root satisfying W^T W = \Sigma^{-1}.

properties.property: Cholesky whitening uses W = L^T, where L is the Cholesky decomposition of \Sigma^{-1}.
properties.why: Matrix factorization satisfying W^T W = L L^T = \Sigma^{-1}.

properties.property: PCA whitening is obtained via the eigen-system of \Sigma.
properties.why: Commonly used choice derived from the eigensystem of the covariance matrix.

properties.property: The unique optimal whitening transformation maximizing component-wise correlation between X and Y is given by W = P^{-1/2} V^{-1/2}.
properties.why: Singled out by optimizing cross-covariance and cross-correlation between X and Y.

properties.property: Mahalanobis distance is Euclidean after whitening transformation.
properties.why: Transformation maps the covariance structure to the identity matrix.

assumptions.assumption: The covariance matrix \Sigma of the random vector X is non-singular (invertible).
assumptions.breaks_when: Variables are collinear or linearly dependent, causing \Sigma to be singular and \Sigma^{-1} to be undefined.

assumptions.assumption: The random vector X resides in a finite-dimensional space.
assumptions.breaks_when: X is an element of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space where the covariance operator has an unbounded inverse.

failure_modes.signature: Matrix inverse \Sigma^{-1}, \Sigma^{-1/2}, or Cholesky decomposition L fails to exist.
failure_modes.cause: Underlying variables have zero variance or are exact linear combinations of each other.

failure_modes.signature: Only partial standardization is possible rather than full whitening.
failure_modes.cause: The covariance operator on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space H possesses an unbounded inverse.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so matrix_whitening is recorded as a definition
